source_documents.title: Emission from CT State and J-aggregates in a Model Coumarin-Paraben Conjugate: A Spectroscopic Study

reference_evidence_units.quote: CP shows the presence of monomers and J-aggregates in solution phase, as evidenced by dual absorption bands which correspond to the fluorescence excitation spectrum, as well as the emission lifetime values obtained from ps-ns spectroscopic experiments.
reference_evidence_units.subject: CP
reference_evidence_units.statement: Monomer and J-aggregate emission in solution.

reference_evidence_units.quote: Excitation of the monomers leads to solvatochromism in the excited state of the monomer
reference_evidence_units.subject: CP

reference_evidence_units.quote: the excitation of J-aggregates in solution leads to solvent independent emission
reference_evidence_units.subject: CP
reference_evidence_units.statement: J-aggregate emission (~600 nm) does not depend on solvent.

reference_evidence_units.quote: the solid-state spectrodynamics of CP is dominated by the H- and J-aggregates along with the monomeric forms of CP
reference_evidence_units.subject: CP
reference_evidence_units.statement: Solid-state emission from H-/J-aggregates and monomers.

reference_mechanisms.label: ICT_TICT_CT
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Monomer emission comes from a solvatochromic CT state (7-diethylaminocoumarin donor-acceptor).

reference_mechanisms.label: AGGREGATE_EXCITON_EXCIMER
reference_mechanisms.rationale: J- (and in the solid, H-) aggregate emission is one of the two emission sources in the title and conclusion.
